BERLIN. Three persons were killed during the night in brawls between Communists and Fascists going home from their political meetings in various parts of Berlin.  Such clashes have become so frequent that the police have forbidden meetings of the hostile parties to be held simultaneously.

BOMBAY. Mrs.  Sarojini Naidu was sentenced to nine months of simple imprisonment as leader of the Gandhi salt raiders at Dharsana Wednesday.
MANCHESTER. Charles Dawes, American ambassador, today was given the honorary degree of Doctor of Laws of Manchester University.  He was one of several upon whom the honor was conferred.
MISS AMY JOHNSON has reached Port Darwin, the first woman to fly alone from England to Australia.

DARWIN. Miss Amy Johnson, 23-year-old English flier, reached this city this afternoon from Atamboea, Timor, after a flight of 400 miles across the adjacent sea.  In reaching her destination, she has completed a 19 day flight from England to her destination.

LONDON. George Lambert, speaking for the liberals in debate on the naval treaty, today supported the government, thus assuring a government majority on the treaty question.

BOMBAY. Nationalist leaders today foresaw increasing cooperation of Moslem elements in the civil disobedience campaign by which they expect to win independence from Great Britain.  A mile long procession of Moslems last night paraded the street to demonstrate Mohammedan sympathy for the movement.

LONDON. The Labor government of Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald today won its second victory within the span of a week by defeating a House of Lords amendment 20 votes to 220.  Just a week ago today the Labor government beat off a conservative motion with a majority of 20, the vote being 270 against 241.
